title: The Oxen and the Butchers

full_text:
The oxen of the land assembled in a vast herd to plan a war of extermination against the butchers, who slaughtered their kind daily. They sharpened their horns and prepared to stampede upon the city.

A wise old ox, who had plowed the fields for many seasons, stepped forward and addressed the herd:

"Pause, brothers, and consider! The butchers slaughter us with practiced hands and sharp blades, ending our lives with swiftness. But if we destroy the butchers, men will still eat beef, and they will employ clumsy, inexperienced laborers who will hack us to pieces with dull axes, prolonging our agony tenfold! Better to endure the skilled master than suffer under the ignorant amateur!"
moral: Beware lest in destroying a known evil you invite an untried and harsher calamity.
